Chronal echo event schedule

Let the crew clock move forward for 5 minutes, while the remote event coordinate is asked to run back through 2,000 years. The slope is the demanded mapping; a physical metric and field solution must still produce it.

Science-fiction premise: the information field follows a continuous future-directed path through a CTC. Its local proper time advances all along the route, even though the chosen Earth-time coordinate can decrease on one segment. Entangled correlations help prepare and compare the field state; they do not carry the message or create that path.

Model limits. The static, spherical Morris–Thorne example is a geometry-to-stress calculation only. It has no clock offset, rotating mouth, time-dependent source, stability analysis, quantum inequality solver, or crew interface. Its negative energy is a major unresolved source problem. The straight line in the event plot specifies a desired schedule, not a computed spacetime trajectory.
